name: Treaty with the Potawatomi, December 17, 1834 (Mota's band)
aka: Treaty of the Indian Agency, Logansport, with Mota and his band
promises: Article 1: the band ceded the four sections reserved for it by Article 2 of the treaty of October 27, 1832.
Article 2: the band would give up possession and remove west of the Mississippi within three years of the ratification of the 1832 treaty.
Article 3: the United States would remove the band to its new country and furnish goods, farming utensils or other necessary articles as under Article 5 of the treaty of October 26, 1832.
Article 4: $680 in goods at signing (acknowledged as received) and $600 in cash at the 1835 annuity payment.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or government finding about this band cession was found. The Commission's Potawatomi decisions that were opened (Dockets 15-P, 29-N and 306 on the 1832 Tippecanoe cession; Docket 128 et al. on other Indiana and Michigan cessions; Docket 15-D et al.) value Royce areas 98, 110, 132, 133, 145, 146, 177, 180 and 181 and do not mention this band reserve.

openQuestions: Whether the $600 due in 1835 was paid and whether the band was removed at United States expense was not traced.

Article 1 refers to a treaty of October 27, 1832 while Article 3 refers to the treaty of October 26, 1832; treaties.json also lists Mota's band and area 201 under the October 27, 1832 treaty (kappler-380). The text is recorded as printed.

Whether the Indian Claims Commission or the Court of Claims ever valued the small 1834 to 1837 band reserve cessions in Indiana was not found; the Potawatomi of Indiana and Michigan dockets (29-K and related) and the Commission's 1978 Final Report docket list should be checked.

The Forest County Potawatomi list the 1834 and 1836 band treaties on their treaty pages but give no account of them; which present-day nations descend from this band was not confirmed (treaties.json names the Citizen Potawatomi Nation).
